full_text:
The 2026 NFL season is just around the corner, which means more NFL player props are being released with each passing week. I previously broke down the [2026 NFL Receiving Touchdown Props](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-player-props-receiving-touchdowns), and it’s time to dive into the 2026 NFL Receiving Touchdowns Leader odds for the top wide receivers and tight ends. In this article, I highlighted a bet I’ve already dropped in our Betting Discord and a couple of additional wagers I considered.

__Davante Adams__ led the league with 14 receiving TDs last season, easily beating a group of four players who finished three touchdowns behind him. __Ja’Marr Chase__ paced the NFL in receiving TDs two seasons ago, and [our subscribers cashed in +1800 odds](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2024/most-receiving-touchdowns-odds#/) on him in this article! Adams, Chase, and __Amon-Ra St. Brown__ are co-favorites to lead the league in receiving touchdowns in 2026 at +700 odds. The three favorites are followed by __Puka Nacua__ (+1000), __Jaxon Smith-Njigba__ (+1000), and __CeeDee Lamb__ (+1500) at 15/1 odds or shorter.

\>Be sure to check out [Brolley’s Best Bets: 2026 NFL Futures](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/series/2025/best-bets) for my favorite futures bets all offseason…Subscribe to the Best Bets Podcast on your [favorite platform](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/podcasts/show/nfl-best-bets) and on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@FantasyPointsBetting) for year-round NFL betting talk…Join our “#official-bets” [Fantasy Points Discord](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/discord) to see our staff's wagers as soon as we make them!

#### __Historical Hints__

We have odds for the last nine years at our disposal, and the league leader in receiving touchdowns has come from all over the odds board. __DeAndre Hopkins__ (+3300), __Kenny Golladay__ (+6500), __Cooper Kupp__ (+6600), and __Mike Evans__ (+3000) each hit at +3000 odds or longer. __Antonio Brown__ (+420), __Davante Adams__ (+800/+900/+1000), and __Ja’Marr Chase__ (+1000) led the league as chalkier options at 10/1 odds or shorter.

Adams is the only player in the last decade to lead the league in receiving TDs more than once, and he’s done it three times in the last six seasons. Chase was the youngest leader in the last nine years at 24 years old, but the leader has been 27 years old or younger in five of the last six seasons. The NFL’s receiving touchdown leader has reached 13+ touchdowns in eight of the last nine years.

Brolley’s Leans
---------------

#### __{{Davante Adams|WR|LAR|16470}}__ (LAR) most regular season receiving touchdowns (+700, BetMGM)

+ __Why I like Adams__: He’s led the league in receiving touchdowns in three of the last six seasons, including his first season with the Rams. He easily paced the league with 14 TDs, which was three more scores than the next closest receivers despite missing three games for a hamstring injury. Adams has reached double-digit touchdowns seven times in his 12-year career, including a dozen or more scores five times. Sean McVay changed his stripes around the goal line with Adams added to the mix last season, ranking behind only the Vikings and Panthers in pass rate over expectation from inside the 5-yard line (9.3%). McVay’s approach helped Adams to easily lead the league with 27 end-zone targets, which was NINE more EZ targets than the next closest receivers, George Pickens and Trey McBride. Adams averaged a ridiculous 1.93 EZ targets/game last season, and he owns the most overall EZ targets (76) and the second-most EZ targets/game (.97) in the *Fantasy Points Data* era (2021-25).

+ __Why I ultimately passed__: It’s tough to bet a +700 favorite in such a large-field market, especially in a stat category that can be extremely noisy from season to season. Adams has proven there are receivers with the ability to consistently score more touchdowns than the rest of the league, but he’s prone to droughts like other receivers after scoring 8 TDs in both 2023 and 2024. The Rams could regress to a more neutral approach at the goal line after ranking 23rd in PROE from inside the 10-yard line (-6.6%) in 2024. Adams missed three games in each of his last two seasons because of hamstring issues. He posted a 77% route share in 2025, but McVay could monitor Adams’ routes more closely entering his age-34 season to try to keep him available for a potential Super Bowl run.

#### __{{Nico Collins|WR|HOU|21756}}__ (Hou) most regular season receiving touchdowns (+5000, BetMGM)

+ __Why I like Collins__: He’s been one of the NFL’s best receivers when he’s healthy over the last three seasons, averaging 5.4 receptions and 86.1 receiving YPG in the 38 games he’s played more than half of the snaps. He can score from anywhere on the field, notching a third of his 21 scores from 28+ yards away in the last three seasons. Collins finished tied for seventh with 12 end-zone targets last season, which he converted into 4 TDs. The Texans ranked 11th in PROE from inside the 5-yard line (2.5%) in Nick Caley’s first season as a playcaller, and they rank seventh in PROE from that range (4.5%) since 2023, when Collins recorded his first of three straight 1000-yard seasons.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Collins’ biggest issue has been staying healthy for an entire season, which he’s yet to do in his first five years. He’s missed nine games since breaking out in 2023, and he’s failed to reach half the snaps in another four games over that span. The Texans could regress to a more neutral approach at the goal line after acquiring David Montgomery. He scored 33 rushing TDs with the Lions over the last three seasons, including 22 times on 52 attempts from inside the 5-yard line. Sportsbooks believe Houston will lean heavily on its top-ranked defense to win games. The Texans rank 22nd in implied team total at 21.9 PPG, which is the lowest total for any of the 16 teams with a 9.5 win total or better.

#### __{{Emeka Egbuka|WR|TB|26092}}__ (TB) most regular season receiving touchdowns (+8000, BetMGM)

+ __Why I like Egbuka__: The Buccaneers surprised most around the league by selecting Egbuka 19th overall last spring despite having an already loaded WR corps. He came out of the gates on fire, ranking behind only Amon-Ra St. Brown with 5 TDs through the first five weeks of his rookie season. Egbuka finished tied for 12th with 11 end-zone targets, but he converted just two of those looks into touchdowns. He’s the top candidate to become Mayfield’s #1 WR after Mike Evans left in free agency, especially with Chris Godwin’s play declining entering his 30s. Baker Mayfield ranked seventh in end-zone attempts (35) last season and is behind only Jared Goff with 95 passing TDs since he became Tampa Bay’s starter in 2023.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Egbuka started his rookie season scorching hot, but scored only 1 TD in his final 12 games. He averaged 2.71 YPRR with a 65.8% catch rate during his hot start before dipping to 1.50 YPRR with a 42.7% catch rate from Week 6 through the end of the season, which coincided with Mayfield struggling through injuries. Egbuka is the top candidate to be the #1 target, but Mayfield could spread the ball around to Godwin and Jalen McMillan under new playcaller __Zac Robinson__. The Falcons ranked 30th in PROE from inside the 10-yard line (-14.4%) the last two seasons under Robinson.

#### __{{Chris Olave|WR|NO|22565}}__ (NO) most regular season receiving touchdowns (+10000, BetMGM)

+ __Why I like Olave__: He owns surprisingly long odds for a receiver coming off a 9-TD campaign in his fourth season, which included six scores once Tyler Shough entered the lineup. Olave finished behind only Davante Adams, George Pickens, and Trey McBride with 14 end-zone targets, scoring on five of those looks. He did it despite the Saints ranking 32nd in PROE from inside the 10-yard line (-17.6%) from Week 8 through the end of the season, once Shough entered the lineup. The Saints ranked 11th overall in PROE with Shough as the starter, so chances are __Kellen Moore__ will call more pass plays closer to the goal line even after signing Travis Etienne. Olave added [8 to 10 pounds](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/nfl-ota-news-tracker#/) this offseason to help him command more goal-line looks after playing on the lighter side for the position early in his career.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Olave stayed relatively healthy last season, but he dealt with multiple concussions earlier in his career. The Saints and Olave could play it on the safe side if he suffered another one this season, especially considering his history. Olave missed the last game of the regular season because of a blood clot in his lung, which had him on blood thinners until the end of June. I’m bullish on the Saints offense this summer, but sportsbooks remain skeptical that the Saints will break through to become a top-10 offense with an implied team total of 21.2 PPG, which ranks 24th. Olave lost his main competition for targets when the Saints traded Rashid Shaheed right as Shough entered the lineup, but they used the eighth overall pick on Jordyn Tyson, who will immediately siphon targets away.

Brolley’s Best Bets
-------------------

{{PAYWALL}}

#### __{{Tee Higgins|WR|CIN|21690}}__ (Cin) most regular season receiving touchdowns (+2000, BetMGM)

\>Risk .3 units to win 6 units. [Placed July 3](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/brolleys-best-bets-nfl-futures).

We’re projecting __Ja’Marr Chase__ to lead the league with 9.1 receiving touchdowns, and his teammate is just two spots behind in third with 8.4 projected TDs. Chase’s odds are much shorter at +700, but Higgins will be in the mix to challenge for the league lead with better injury luck. Higgins missed seven games over the last two seasons, but ranks fourth in receiving TDs (21) and behind only __Davante Adams__ in receiving TDs/game (.78) in that span. Higgins wins at all levels of the field and is a dominant perimeter option at 6’4”, 220 pounds, and he’s been better than Chase in the TD department on a per-target and per-route basis the last two seasons. Higgins scored 21 times on 200 targets (9.5%) and 924 routes (2.3%), compared to 25 scores on 353 targets (7.1%) and 698 routes (1.9%) for Chase.

The Bengals ranked seventh in PROE from inside the 10-yard line (5.3%) last season after ranking second (16.8%) in 2024. Higgins tied for seventh with 12 end-zone targets last season, which came a year after he led the league with 1.25 EZ targets/game in 2024. Burrow ranked fourth with 2.50 end-zone attempts/game last season, and is pacing the league over the last two seasons at 3.20. The Bengals threw the second-most passing TDs (36) last season and have the fifth-highest implied team total at 25.5 PPG entering 2026. Higgins will stay busy at the goal line, and he just needs to stay healthy to vie for the touchdown crown.

#### __{{Mike Evans|WR|SF|16597}}__ (SF) most regular season receiving touchdowns (+4000, BetMGM)

\>Risk .2 units to win 8 units. [Placed July 3](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/brolleys-best-bets-nfl-futures).

We already bet on Evans to clear [5.5 receiving touchdowns](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-player-props-receiving-touchdowns), and I’m digging his longshot odds to lead the league in receiving touchdowns for the second time in his 30s. He previously paced the league with 13 TDs at 30 years old in 2023, which was the sixth time in 12 seasons he reached 11+ TDs. We have to go back to just last season for a 33-year-old WR to lead the league in receiving TDs in his first season with a new team, when __Davante Adams__ did it with __Sean McVay__ and __Matthew Stafford__. Evans joined a new team for the first time at 33 years old, opting for an upgrade at playcaller (__Kyle Shanahan__) and quarterback (__Brock Purdy__).

​​Evans is still a matchup nightmare at all three levels of the field because of his size (6’5”, 231 pounds), speed, and physicality. He finished sixth in aDOT (14.1), eighth in TPRR (.28), and second in A.S.S. (.147) behind only Adams and just ahead of OPOY __Jaxon Smith-Njigba__. However, he ranked 67th in catchable target rate (67.8%) with __Baker Mayfield__ struggling through injuries under one-and-done playcaller __Josh Grizzard__. Evans shouldn’t have the same issues with Purdy, who ranked fifth in catchable throw rate (78.9%) under Shanahan, whose passing game finished behind only the Patriots in success rate (54.2%).

Purdy owns an elite 6.2% TD rate through four seasons, which ranks behind only __Lamar Jackson__ (6.5%) among active QBs. The 49ers ranked sixth in PROE from inside the 10-yard line (5.7%) last season without Evans in the mix, and Purdy tied for fifth with 2.44 end-zone attempts per game last season. Evans saw just 7 end-zone targets (.88 per game) in his final season with the Buccaneers after posting 36 EZ targets in his first 31 games (1.16) with Mayfield in 2023-24. He should get plenty of opportunities to score in a 49ers offense that produced the fourth-most passing TDs (33) last season as long as he has a little better injury luck — he missed just eight games in his first 10 seasons before missing 12 games in the last two seasons.
